:::{#exm-floor}
#### Floors

- $\floor{2.7} = 2$, by the [definition of the floor](#def-floor).
- $\floor{3} = 3$,
  because $3$ is already an [integer](#def-integers).
- $\floor{-1.5} = -2$,
  because $-2 \le -1.5 < -1$.

The [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) of $\floor{x}$ is a staircase:
each step starts at an integer, with a filled dot,
and stops before the next integer, at an open dot.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The graph of the floor function from -3 to 3. It is a staircase of
#|   horizontal steps one unit long. Each step starts with a filled dot at an
#|   integer k at height k and ends with an open dot at k + 1.

# one step per integer k, from x = k to x = k + 1 at height k
k <- -3:2
steps <- tibble::tibble(x = k, xend = k + 1, y = k)

floor_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(steps) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(ggplot2::aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y), size = 2) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(x = xend, y = y),
    size = 2, shape = 21, fill = "white"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "floor of x")

floor_plot
```

:::
